{{Infobox Election | election_name = United States House of Representatives elections in Oklahoma, 2018 | country = Oklahoma | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Oklahoma, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | next_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Oklahoma, 2020 | next_year = 2020 | seats_for_election = All 5 Oklahoma seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | party1 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election1 = 5 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election2 = 0 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = | map_image = | map_caption = }} {{ElectionsOK}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Oklahoma''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the 5 [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Oklahoma]], one from each of the state's 5 [[Oklahoma's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2016|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[United States Senate elections, 2016|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[United States elections, 2016#State elections|state]] and [[United States elections, 2016#Local elections|local elections]]. Primary elections were held on June 26 and runoff elections were held two months later on August 28.{{cite web |title=Oklahoma Elections — 2018 |url=https://www.ok.gov/elections/Election_Info/2018_Election_Calendar.html |website=Oklahoma State Election Board |publisher=The State of Oklahoma |accessdate=20 August 2018}} {{Toclimit|limit=2}} ==District 1== {{see also|Oklahoma's 1st congressional district}} The 1st district is located in the [[Tulsa metropolitan area]] and includes [[Creek County, Oklahoma|Creek]], [[Rogers County, Oklahoma|Rogers]], [[Tulsa County, Oklahoma|Tulsa]], [[Wagoner County, Oklahoma|Wagoner]] and [[Washington County, Oklahoma|Washington]] counties. The incumbent was Republican [[Jim Bridenstine]], who had represented the district since 2013. He was re-elected unopposed in the general election and with 81% of the vote in the Republican primary. During his initial election in 2012, Bridenstine self-imposed a three term limit. Bridenstine has confirmed he will honor his term-limit pledge.{{cite web|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/news/government/congressman-jim-bridenstine-says-third-term-would-be-his-last/article_2f48f417-49c1-5231-86a7-2031e3346ff1.html|title=Congressman Jim Bridenstine says third term would be his last|work=[[Tulsa World]]|last=Krehbiel|first=Randy|date=November 10, 2015|accessdate=November 22, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/after-ho-hum-year-for-state-political-contests-2018-will-be-transformational/article/5522614|title=After ho-hum year for state political contests, 2018 will be 'transformational'|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|last=Casteel|first=Chris|date=October 17, 2016|accessdate=November 4, 2016}} Bridenstine has become [[List of Administrators and Deputy Administrators of NASA|Administrator]] of [[NASA]] in the Donald Trump administration.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/powerpost/wp/2016/11/11/gop-congressman-being-considered-for-nasa-administrator-in-trump-administration/|title=GOP congressman being considered for NASA The incumbent is Republican [[Markwayne Mullin]], who has represented the district since 2013. He was re-elected with 71% of the vote in 2016. Mullin had pledged to serve only three terms when he was first elected in 2012. During the 2016 campaign, Mullin stated he was reassessing his pledge, and refused to rule out running again in 2018.{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/article/5488459|title=Oklahoma Congressman Mullin The largest district in Oklahoma and one of the largest in the country, it includes the [[Oklahoma Panhandle]], [[Ponca City, Oklahoma|Ponca City]] and the city of [[Stillwater, Oklahoma|Stillwater]] as well as the [[Osage Nation]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Frank Lucas (Oklahoma politician)|Frank Lucas]], who has represented the district since 2003 and previously represented the 6th district from 1994 to 2003.
